newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria offers two pharmaceutical plants for sale.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria offers two pharmaceutical plants for sale.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet approved the privatisation of two major pharmaceutical plants, the Dupnitsa-based Pharmatsia and Troyapharm in Troyan in a bid boost budget revenue, a government spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
"The cabinet agreed to privatise 55 percent of Pharamatsia and Troyapharm," the spokeswoman told journalists. She gave no further details.
The government retains a 25 percent stake in each of the firms.
Pharmatsia's sales last year amounted to 1.14 billion levs and 31 percent of its produce was exported to Germany, the Middle East, Hungary, Poland and Russia. The company employes 2,500 people.
Balkanfarma, a local pharmaceutics company, has offered to the Privatisation Agency $24.6 million for the stake in Pharmatsia, local media said recently.
Troyafarm B, a firm set up by Troyafarm's management, has offered $10.9 million for the stake in Troyafarm, newspapers said.
Troyafarm is a local monopolist of life-saving infusion solutions among other medicines. Its sales last year amounted to 1.4 billion levs and 30 percent of its products were exported.
The Privatisation Agency declined comment on the possible deals before they were concluded.
The government pledged to sell off some 20 major state enteprises in the next few months, hoping to raise cash for foreign debt payments.
